statement: In $\triangle ABC$, $P \in BC$. Circle $S_1$ centered at $B$ through $P$ meets $AB$ at $D$; circle $S_2$ centered at $C$ through $P$ meets $AC$ at $E$. Line $AP$ meets $S_1$ at $X$ and $S_2$ at $Y$ ($\neq P$). $T = DX \cap EY$. Prove $\angle BAC + 2\angle DTE = 180^\circ$.

Let $a, b, c$ be pairwise coprime positive integers. For each $n \geq 1$, let $s(n)$ = number of elements of $\{a,b,c\}$ dividing $n$. Let $k_1 < k_2 < \cdots$ be all positive integers divisible by some element of $\{a,b,c\}$. The characteristic sequence of $(a,b,c)$ is $s(k_1), s(k_2), \ldots$ Prove that equal characteristic sequences imply $\{a,b,c\} = \{a',b',c'\}$.
$n \geq 1$ is \textit{conservative} if the smallest prime divisor of $(n!)^n + 1$ is at most $n + 2015$. Is the number of conservative integers finite or infinite?

A $9 \times 9$ board has some cells painted black. A coloring is \textit{good} if there exists a white starting square from which a chip can return to the start, moving through white squares, visiting at least 3 squares without repetition. Find the maximum $k$ such that any coloring of $k$ cells black is good.
For positive integer $n$, let $d(n) = \gcd\!\left\{\binom{n+1}{n}, \binom{n+2}{n}, \ldots, \binom{2n}{n}\right\}$. Find all possible values of $d(n)$.

In $\triangle ABC$ with incenter $I$, circumcenter $O$, and inradius $r$: $A_1 \in \omega$ (incircle) makes $AIA_1O$ a convex trapezoid with bases $AO$ and $IA_1$. Circle $\omega_1$ (radius $r$, through $A_1$, tangent to $AB$, $\neq \omega$) and $\omega_2$ (radius $r$, through $A_1$, tangent to $AC$, $\neq \omega$) meet at $A_1$ and $A_2$. Define $B_2$, $C_2$ similarly. Prove $AA_2$, $BB_2$, $CC_2$ concurrent.
